title: Triples With Bitwise AND Equal to Zero
description: Given an integer array `nums` where every element lies in `[0, 2^16 - 1]`, return the number of ordered index triples `(i, j, k)` (`0 <= i, j, k < nums.length`) such that `(nums[i] & nums[j] & nums[k]) == 0`.
hints: First count how many ordered pairs `(i, j)` produce each pairwise AND value `v = nums[i] & nums[j]` in an array `dp[v]` of size `2^B` (grouping duplicate values of `nums` speeds this up further).
Run Sum Over Subsets (SOS) DP on `dp` so `dp[mask]` stores the count of pairs whose AND is a submask of `mask`; then for each `x` in `nums`, add `dp[((1 << B) - 1) ^ x]`.

examples.explanation: There are 12 ordered index triples in [2, 1, 3] whose bitwise AND is 0.
Every one of the 3^3 = 27 triples in [0, 0, 0] has bitwise AND 0.
Every triple in [1, 1] has bitwise AND 1 != 0, so the count is 0.
